I've been working this land for 45 years. Quzhou is dry country — the well is everything. My wife and I can only do so much, so I keep things simple and stick to what I know works on this soil.

I'll split the land the way I always have: 8 mu for cotton — that's my main income — and the other 5.5 mu I double-crop with winter wheat going in after autumn and summer maize coming right after wheat harvest in June. That system feeds us and brings in extra cash.

For cotton, I switched to Bt hybrid seeds years ago. Saves me money on bollworm spraying, though I still spray for aphids and spider mites. I put down heavy nitrogen — cotton needs it — split into base and two topdresses. I irrigate five times through the season, starting before planting to set the seedbed. I rotary-till before transplanting, same as always.

For wheat, I use improved certified seed from the county ag station. I plough the cotton stubble under in October to bury disease. Four irrigations — sowing water, winter water, jointing, and grain fill. That's the minimum I can get away with here.

Maize I direct-seed straight into wheat stubble. No tillage — saves time and the soil holds moisture better. Hybrid seed, good yield. I only need to irrigate a few times since the summer rains help.
